Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) can also provide stage-1 scores for 2S-PA.
The important requirement is to retain the measurement-error covariance of
the scores, rather than treating the scores as perfectly measured.

This vignette uses a five-factor EFA of personality items from `psych::bfi`.
We calculate Bartlett scores with `psych::factor.scores()`, obtain their
measurement-error covariance with `R2spa::compute_fscore()`, and use that
information to estimate latent correlations in stage 2. Because EFA allows
cross-loadings, the factor interpretation depends on the selected rotation.

```{r}
library(psych)
data(bfi, package = "psych")
library(lavaan)
```

## Example: Big Five Inventory

The first 25 variables contain five items for each of the Big Five domains.
We use a target rotation that encourages the expected five-domain loading
pattern while allowing cross-loadings. The measurement model is estimated
from the complete-case item correlation matrix.

```{r}
# Complete-case (listwise) correlation — the same rows used to compute the
# scores below, so stage 1 (EFA) and stage 2 (2S-PA) share one data basis.
cc <- complete.cases(bfi[, 1:25])
corr_bfi <- cor(bfi[cc, 1:25])
# EFA (Target rotation)
target_mat_bfi <- matrix(0, nrow = 25, ncol = 5)
target_mat_bfi[1:5, 1] <- NA
target_mat_bfi[6:10, 2] <- NA
target_mat_bfi[11:15, 3] <- NA
target_mat_bfi[16:20, 4] <- NA
target_mat_bfi[21:25, 5] <- NA
fa_target_bfi <- psych::fa(
    corr_bfi, n.obs = sum(cc),
    nfactors = 5,
    rotate = "targetQ", Target = target_mat_bfi,
    scores = "Bartlett",
    n.rotations = 1)
# Factor correlations
fa_target_bfi$Phi |>
    (`[`)(paste0("MR", 1:5), paste0("MR", 1:5)) |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "EFA Factor Correlation")
```

```{r}
# Correlation with sum scores
bfi |>
    transform(A = (7 - A1) + A2 + A3 + A4 + A5,
           C = C1 + C2 + C3 + (7 - C4) + (7 - C5),
           E = (7 - E1) + (7 - E2) + E3 + E4 + E5,
           N = N1 + N2 + N3 + N4 + N5,
           O = O1 + (7 - O2) + O3 + O4 + (7 - O5)) |>
    subset(select = A:O) |>
    cor(use = "complete") |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Sum scores")
```

### From item weights to factor scores

A Bartlett score is a weighted combination of the standardized items.
The next calculation illustrates the score for the first participant
and compares it with the score returned by `psych`:

```{r}
# Bartlett score for first person
bscores <-
    psych::factor.scores(bfi[, 1:25], f = fa_target_bfi,
                         method = "Bartlett")
fa_target_bfi$weights
# Calculation by hand
y1 <- scale(bfi[, 1:25])[1, ]  # z-score
crossprod(fa_target_bfi$weights, as.matrix(y1))
# Compare to results from psych::fa()
bscores$scores[1, ]
```

```{r}
# Covariance of Bartlett scores
cov(bscores$scores, use = "complete") |>
    (`[`)(paste0("MR", 1:5), paste0("MR", 1:5)) |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "With Bartlett scores")
```

### Obtain the score measurement-error covariance

`compute_fscore()` takes the estimated item loadings and unique variances
directly. Here, `theta` is a diagonal matrix of EFA uniquenesses, and
`fs_matrices = TRUE` requests the score measurement matrices in addition
to the scores. The standardized data are already centered, so we set
`center_y = FALSE`.

```{r}
# Obtain error covariances
yc <- scale(bfi[, 1:25])
yc <- yc[complete.cases(yc), ]
lam <- fa_target_bfi$loadings
colnames(lam) <- c("N", "E", "C", "A", "O")
phi <- fa_target_bfi$Phi
th <- diag(fa_target_bfi$uniquenesses)
# # scoring weights
# a <- solve(crossprod(lam, solve(th, lam)), t(solve(th, lam)))
# ecov_fs <- a %*% th %*% t(a)
# dimnames(ecov_fs) <- rep(list(c("N", "E", "C", "A", "O")), 2)
# Two-stage analysis
library(R2spa)
bfi_fs <- compute_fscore(yc, lambda = lam, theta = th,
                         method = "Bartlett", center_y = FALSE,
                         fs_matrices = TRUE)
head(bfi_fs)
# Scoring matrix
attr(bfi_fs, which = "scoring_matrix")
# Error covariance
attr(bfi_fs, which = "fsT")
```

### Estimate latent correlations with 2S-PA

For Bartlett scores, the score loading matrix is the identity. We supply
it together with the error covariance obtained above. An empty structural
model string leaves the latent covariances unrestricted in this example.

```{r}
ts_fit <- tspa("",
               data = data.frame(bscores$scores) |>
                   setNames(c("fs_N", "fs_E", "fs_C", "fs_A", "fs_O")),
               fsT = attr(bfi_fs, which = "fsT"),
               fsL = diag(5) |>
                   `dimnames<-`(list(c("fs_N", "fs_E", "fs_C", "fs_A", "fs_O"),
                                     c("N", "E", "C", "A", "O"))))
lavInspect(ts_fit, what = "cor.lv") |>
    (`[`)(c("A", "C", "E", "N", "O"), c("A", "C", "E", "N", "O")) |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "With Bartlett scores and 2S-PA")
```

Compare the resulting latent correlation matrix with the EFA factor
correlations and with the correlations of the uncorrected scores.
The latter describe relations among fallible scores; the 2S-PA correlations
account for their estimated measurement error. The EFA specification and
rotation remain part of the measurement assumptions underlying that correction.
